Where it began

Pathum Nissanka was born in Galle on 18 May 1998. He took up the game seriously at Kalutara Vidyalaya before moving to Isipathana College in Colombo, and as a schoolboy he once made an unbeaten 205 from 190 balls against President's College.

The runs kept coming once he left school. In the 2018–19 Premier League Tournament he made 1,088 for Nondescripts in only seven matches, and early in 2019 he was Sri Lanka A's top scorer in a two-match first-class series against Ireland A.

The player

His Test debut came against the West Indies on 21 March 2021, and he marked it with 103 in the second innings. He was only the fourth Sri Lankan to score a hundred on Test debut, and the first to do it away from home.

Back in the side against England in 2024, he steered a chase of 219 with an unbeaten 127 from 124 balls, giving Sri Lanka their first Test win over England for ten years. Later, against Bangladesh, he made 187 for his first Test hundred on home soil, then another hundred in the next Test as Sri Lanka won by an innings. By November 2026 he had played 19 Tests, scoring 1,310 runs at 42.26 with four hundreds and seven fifties, and had taken 12 catches.

What made him special

He was an opener who could adapt to any length of game. In February 2024 he made 210 not out against Afghanistan, the first ODI double hundred by a Sri Lankan, and in September 2025 he added a T20 international hundred against India. That gave him the rare set of a Test hundred, an ODI double and a T20 hundred. He went on to become the first Sri Lankan with more than one T20 international century.

Test cricket did make him wait. At one stage he went two years without a Test, and he came back as if he had never been away. Patience, it seems, was part of his game, though the eight sixes in that double hundred suggest it had its limits.

Away from the middle

He was part of the side that won the 2022 Asia Cup, opening with Kusal Mendis. The ICC picked him in its ODI Team of the Year for 2024, and Sri Lanka Cricket named him its Cricketer of the Year for 2025, along with its Test and T20 batting awards that year. He also played franchise cricket in the Lanka Premier League and, from 2026, the IPL with Delhi Capitals.

And finally

As a schoolboy he made 205 not out. Years later, playing for his country, he made 210 not out. It is a gentle reminder that the boys who make big hundreds at school sometimes simply carry on doing it, only in front of more people.
